findings.stage: started an order → paid and confirmed
segments: customers with 2 or more items in cart
findings.hypothesis: Carts with a single item convert much better (139,707 of 315,934, 44.22%) than multi‑item carts (e.g. 3–5 items convert 43,996 of 176,399, 24.94%); if every cart converted like single‑item carts we would see ~56,509 more paid orders (286,131 expected vs 229,622 actual), so multi‑item behavior explains the largest recoverable chunk of the 417,569 lost.
findings.confirm_via: Run a holdout A/B test that (a) offers free/discounted shipping or a one‑click checkout button to a random subset of multi‑item carts and (b) measures paid-and-confirmed conversions by item_count. If conversions on treated multi‑item carts rise toward the single‑item baseline, the shipping/checkout friction hypothesis is confirmed.

findings.stage: started an order → paid and confirmed
segments: orders that did not need a prescription
findings.hypothesis: Carts that need a prescription convert worse (76,641 of 255,293, 30.02%) than non‑prescription carts (152,981 of 391,898, 39.04%); if rx_gated carts converted like non_rx carts we would recover roughly 22,998 paid orders, so prescription gating/consultation steps are a meaningful contributor to the 417,569 loss.
findings.confirm_via: Experimentally streamline the prescription path for a random subset of rx_gated carts (e.g., one‑tap 'Book a consult now' inline with checkout, auto‑attach consult outcome into the order flow) and measure whether paid-and-confirmed conversions rise versus control.

findings.stage: started an order → paid and confirmed
segments: orders with all items in stock
orders with at least one item unfulfillable or partially fulfillable
findings.hypothesis: Orders with unfulfilled or partially fulfilled items perform extremely poorly (1,831 of 19,728, 9.28% and 16 of 2,191, 0.73% respectively) versus orders where all items are in stock (217,230 of 594,507, 36.54%); bringing those buckets up to the all‑items‑fulfilled rate could recover ~6,158 paid orders, so inventory/fulfillment gating explains a small but acute portion of the loss.
findings.confirm_via: Run an experiment that (a) offers automatic substitution suggestions or a 'notify and hold' option for orders with unfulfilled items, and (b) measures paid-and-confirmed conversions for affected orders versus current behavior.

findings.stage: started an order → paid and confirmed
findings.hypothesis: Conversion varies by hour; high‑volume evening hours (for example 17:00 with 34,090 started and 30.70% conversion) are below the best hour (00:00 at 46.40%, though low volume). Targeting retries/messaging or payment fallbacks in specific evening hours could recover a few thousand paid orders (roughly 4k estimated from evenings tested), so time‑bound payment/session friction is a secondary factor in the 417,569 loss.
findings.confirm_via: Run time‑targeted experiments that (a) apply a different payment retry logic and clearer messaging for orders started between 17:00–21:00 and (b) measure the paid-and-confirmed lift during those hours versus control.

findings.stage: started an order → paid and confirmed
findings.hypothesis: Recorded reasons show 199,417 user‑side abandon notes (111,993 'user abandon the cart', 83,517 'user clicked back') versus 42,107 artifact reasons; much of the 417,569 loss appears to be voluntary user abandonment rather than platform errors, pointing to UX, price sensitivity or perceived friction at checkout as dominant causes.
findings.confirm_via: Instrument short in‑flow surveys or a microphone/exit intent prompt on the checkout page for abandoning users to collect causal reasons, and run A/B tests of targeted UX fixes (e.g., clearer total price, fewer required fields) to measure conversion impact.

growth_ideas.title: One‑tap express checkout
growth_ideas.rationale: Single‑item carts convert far better (44.22%), so removing friction for rapid repeat purchases should increase paid orders for a large share of traffic.
growth_ideas.description: Add an express 'Buy now' flow for products meeting criteria (single item, saved address, saved card or OTP payment) that skips cart review and completes payment with one confirmation tap; expose it on product pages and the cart for returning users who opt in to saving one payment method and address.
growth_ideas.target_stage: started an order → paid and confirmed

growth_ideas.title: In‑cart prescription fast‑path
growth_ideas.rationale: Prescription‑required carts convert ~9pp worse; reducing the extra steps (consultation, upload) in the cart will raise paid orders among rx_gated users.
growth_ideas.description: Add an inline 'Complete prescription' assistant in the cart that (a) offers immediate teleconsult booking with auto‑attach to the order, (b) allows secure upload and one‑tap acceptance of an existing prescription, and (c) shows ETA for consult and a progress status so users see the path to completion before leaving checkout.
growth_ideas.target_stage: started an order → paid and confirmed

growth_ideas.title: Auto‑substitute and hold for OOS items
growth_ideas.rationale: Orders with unfulfilled items convert extremely poorly; giving customers clear, low‑friction choices when stock problems occur should recover conversions instead of losing the whole order.
growth_ideas.description: When an item is unfulfillable, present two clear, prominent options in checkout: 'Auto‑substitute with nearest equivalent' with pre‑selected pricing and shipping, or 'Hold full order and notify me when all items available' with an ETA; track conversions and fulfillment outcomes for both flows.
growth_ideas.target_stage: started an order → paid and confirmed

growth_ideas.title: Evening payment retry and messaging
growth_ideas.rationale: High‑volume evening hours convert worse than other times; targeted retry logic and clearer payment messaging can recover lost paid orders during those hours.
growth_ideas.description: Implement a time‑aware payment flow that (a) retries failed authorizations silently up to a configurable number during 17:00–21:00 with an immediate fallback to an alternate PSP, and (b) surfaces a compact explainers ('why payment may fail and how to fix') during those hours; A/B test conversion lift in the target window.
growth_ideas.target_stage: started an order → paid and confirmed
